root_cause: The adjustDate function in pikaday.js adds days by adding milliseconds (UTC), which does not account for daylight saving time transitions. When crossing a DST boundary, adding 7 days worth of milliseconds can result in a local date that is off by one day, causing ArrowDown to land on 2026-10-29 instead of the expected 2026-10-30.
repair_strategy: Replace the adjustDate to adjustDate to perform calendar-day arithmetic by manipulating the date's year, month, and day fields. This ensures that adding 7 days moves the local date by exactly 7 calendar days regardless of DST changes. The while loop that skips disabled days (weekends) is also updated to use calendar-day increments.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation for date pickers will correctly move by weeks across DST boundaries, ensuring users can select dates predictably and consistently with WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Changing date arithmetic may affect other uses of adjustDate (e.g., single-day arrows). However, the new method is more correct for all cases.
Risk of off-by-one in other scenarios is low because the Date constructor handles month/year rollover.
verification_requirements: Test ArrowDown on a date before DST end (e.g., 2026-10-22) results in 2026-10-30 (not 2026-10-29).
Test single-day arrows (ArrowLeft/Right) across DST boundaries.
Verify that weekend skipping still works correctly.
